points.text: M1: $\text{ClCH}_2\text{COOH}$ most acidic, then $\text{BrCH}_2\text{COOH}$, then $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$, then $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ least acidic

M2: electron withdrawing groups / electronegative groups / negative inductive effect AND weakens O-H bond / more stable anion OR electron donating groups / positive inductive effect AND strengthens O-H bond / less stable anion

M3: any two of: chlorine is more electron-withdrawing / electronegative than bromine (related to $\text{XCH}_2\text{COOH}$); electron withdrawing of C=O / negative inductive effect of C=O (related to COOH); positive inductive effect / electron donating of alkyl / ethyl / R group (related to ROH)
M4: all three comparative electronic factors explained: chlorine more electronegative than bromine; electron withdrawing of C=O in COOH; electron donating of alkyl / ethyl in ROH
M1: [structure: ---NH-C6H4-NH-CO-CO--- with displayed C=O] correct displayed amide bond with C=O, $(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)-\text{N}$ and $(\text{C}-)\text{C=O}$
M2: rest of the structure correct with continuation bonds
M2: [structure: HO-C6H4-N=N-C6H4-N=N-C6H4-OH] bis-azo dye with two N=N links and two terminal 2-hydroxyphenyl groups and central phenylene
